articles.title: Manchester United shocked as talented youngster JJ Gabriel asks to leave
articles.summary: 15-year-old wants his registration to be cancelled. He was to be in squad to face Brighton on Wednesday. Manchester United have been left confused and shocked by the news that the talented 15-year-old player JJ Gabriel has asked to leave the club, a day before he was to be included in the…
body: Gabriel could have become United’s youngest player in the Carabao Cup third-round tie at Old Trafford on Wednesday. But the Guardian understands he has asked for his registration to be cancelled.

United are unsure what has prompted this decision and believe they have done everything they can to show Gabriel and his family there is a pathway to the first team. Those efforts have included meetings with Ruben Amorim, when the Portuguese was head coach, and Sir Alex Ferguson.

United believe the situation, first reported by the Telegraph, is rectifiable given the time remaining on Gabriel’s contract. Club officials say the player has a deal to the end of the season and cannot be deregistered despite his request. The north London-born Gabriel cannot sign a professional contract until he turns 17 in October next year, but can sign a scholarship agreement when he turns 16.

articles.title: ‘I loved my time in the FBI but nothing can compare to the NFL’: Charles ‘Peanut’ Tillman on his unlikely career path
articles.summary: The player who invented the Peanut Punch talks about his nomadic childhood, love of Chicago and time as a cop. By No Helmets Required. Defensive back Charles Tillman played 168 games for his hometown team Chicago Bears across 13 NFL seasons.
body: You went to a dozen schools around the world as a child. Do you share your own experiences when you coach kids now? “Absolutely. I share a great deal because it helped shape me into the person I am today. My dad being in the military and us moving around so much helped my personality. I’m very outgoing and a lot of that stems from my childhood, always being the new kid in school and having to make new friends. So, I talk about those experiences with the kids when it feels appropriate.”

When you walked into a new classroom full of strangers did you have to force yourself to be extrovert? “No, when I tried to make friends or meet new people, it came from a genuine place. I looked at it as another adventure: ‘Oh, wow, I’ve never been to this country or this state before. Let’s learn about northern California. Let’s learn about West Germany.’ I had a chance to see different cultures and how people lived. ‘OK, this is what they do in Texas. This is how they do it in Louisiana’. I was pretty well rounded. And it made me comfortable being around so many different cultures and ethnicities. I loved it.”

articles.title: Raheem Sterling pleads guilty to dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide
articles.summary: Ex-England footballer also admits to failing to provide a specimen as he appears at Basingstoke magistrates court. The former England footballer Raheem Sterling has admitted dangerously driving a Lamborghini on the motorway.
body: Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke magistrates court on Tuesday to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3 and the A327 before he crashed on 28 May.
The 31-year-old admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.
Sterling attended the Hampshire court wearing a black suit jacket, black trousers, black shoes and a dark top.
Hampshire and Isle of Wight constabulary previously said the charges followed a single-vehicle collision on the M3 southbound, near Minley interchange, on 28 May.

articles.title: Eligibility rules 'not particularly fair' - O'Neill
articles.summary: Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill says what upsets him the most regarding rules over international eligibility is the pressure put on young players to make an irreversible choice.
body: Any player born in Northern Ireland is also eligible to play for the Republic of Ireland, but Fifa rules state that an application to transfer international allegiance can only be made once.

The situation has again been in the spotlight with regards to Arsenal teenager Ceadach O'Neill who has won two senior caps for Northern Ireland and on Tuesday was included in the squad for a Nations League quadruple-header, but has also been subject to an approach from the Republic of Ireland.

At present, the player would be required to undertake a Fifa transfer of international allegiance should he wish to play for the Republic of Ireland at any level, but if he makes an appearance in the upcoming Nations League quadruple header, would have to wait until he is 21 to do so. Should he reach four caps, he would be unable to transfer at any stage.
"My focus is on the player, and I have a duty of care to the player as his international manager, as we have as an association as well," said Michael O'Neill.

articles.title: Celtic & Scotland legend McGrain diagnosed with Alzheimer's
articles.summary: Danny McGrain, described by Celtic as "Scotland's greatest-ever full-back", has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease, his family confirms.
body: Speaking to the club's website, wife Laraine McGrain said she wanted to explain why the 76-year-old had become less involved with the Scottish champions and their fans.
"Danny received this diagnosis some time ago and, as time has moved on, we felt it was right to be open and clear," she said.
"Danny has always loved helping supporters - whether through hospital visits, assisting fans with charity events, or sending messages of support.
"As time has gone on, that has become more difficult for Danny, so we wanted to explain his situation with honesty and with the care and respect the Celtic family has always shown us."

articles.title: London misses out as Nairobi secures 2029 World Athletics Championships
articles.summary: The World Athletics Championships are heading to Africa for the first time after Kenya's capital Nairobi was confirmed as host of the 2029 edition, with London missing out.
body: Kenya has long been a superpower in distance running but has yet to host an event of this scale. The championships will return to Germany in 2031 with Munich hosting.

"We were fortunate to have four outstanding bids for 2029 and 2031, and this was not an easy decision for the council," said World Athletics president Sebastian Coe as he announced the decision following the Ultimate Championship in Hungary.
"The quality, ambition and commitment demonstrated by all four candidates underlines the strength and global appeal of the World Athletics Championships."

Jack Buckner, CEO of UK Athletics and co-founder of Athletic Ventures, said: "We are deeply disappointed that the 2029 World Athletics Championships will not be held in London. We believed we had an outstanding bid which would genuinely take the sport to new levels.

articles.title: McIlroy: I’m not worried by new PGA Tour qualification criteria
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy is unconcerned about the impact the PGA Tour’s new membership criteria for its revamped competitive structure could have on DP World Tour players seeking to earn a card on the US circuit.
body: On Tuesday, the PGA Tour outlined new membership categories for its two-tier promotion-and-relegation structure, launching in 2028.
Under the current PGA Tour qualification structure, the top 10 players finishing at the top of the DP World Tour's Race to Dubai Rankings will win PGA Tour cards for the following season.
However, the PGA Tour did not confirm how many cards will be offered to top performers on the DP World Tour.
The PGA Tour said: "Access available to top performers from the DP World Tour is being considered as part of the ongoing discussions regarding the future of the Strategic Alliance."
